criteria: No visible diabetic retinal abnormalities; absence of microaneurysms, hemorrhages, hard exudates, or cotton wool spots.
clinical_management: Annual dilated fundus screening recommended. Maintain optimal glycemic and blood pressure control.
references: International Council of Ophthalmology (ICO) Guidelines for Diabetic Eye Care.

criteria: Presence of microaneurysms only. No visible retinal hemorrhages, hard exudates, or venous beading.
clinical_management: Follow-up comprehensive eye examination in 6-12 months. Reinforce glycemic, lipid, and blood pressure control.
references: American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO) Preferred Practice Pattern - Diabetic Retinopathy.

criteria: More than just microaneurysms, but less than Severe NPDR. Includes dot-and-blot hemorrhages, hard exudates, and cotton wool spots.
clinical_management: Referral to ophthalmologist. Re-evaluation every 3-6 months. Evaluate for macular edema with OCT if foveal involvement suspected.
references: Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) Report No. 10.

criteria: Meets 4-2-1 rule: severe intraretinal hemorrhages in all 4 quadrants, venous beading in >=2 quadrants, or prominent IRMA in >=1 quadrant.
clinical_management: Urgent retinal specialist referral (within 2-4 weeks). High risk of progression to PDR. Consider panretinal photocoagulation (PRP) or anti-VEGF therapy.
references: ETDRS 4-2-1 Rule Guidelines; AAO Preferred Practice Pattern.

criteria: Neovascularization of the disc (NVD), neovascularization elsewhere (NVE), pre-retinal or vitreous hemorrhage, or fibrovascular proliferation.
clinical_management: Immediate ophthalmic intervention required (within 24-48 hours to 1 week). Panretinal photocoagulation (PRP), anti-VEGF intravitreal injections, or vitrectomy for non-clearing vitreous hemorrhage.
references: Diabetic Retinopathy Study (DRS) & AAO Preferred Practice Pattern.

criteria: Increased vertical cup-to-disc ratio (VCDR > 0.65), neuroretinal rim thinning (notably inferior and superior rims violating ISNT rule), disc hemorrhages, or retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) defects.
clinical_management: Comprehensive glaucoma workup including Goldmann applanation tonometry, gonioscopy, standard automated perimetry (visual field test), and spectral-domain OCT of the optic nerve head. Initiate IOP-lowering topical drops if confirmed.
references: European Glaucoma Society (EGS) Guidelines (5th Edition); AAO Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma PPP.

criteria: Healthy optic nerve head with intact, symmetric neuroretinal rim obeying the ISNT rule; VCDR <= 0.5 without notch, excavation, or disc hemorrhage.
clinical_management: Routine age-appropriate ophthalmic screening every 2 years. Monitor if high myopia or family history present.
